question: On the basis of the track width of Indian Railways, what type of gauge is Matheran Hill Railways?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Narrow gauge**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The small gauge **is called a **Narrow gauge **or a small** line**.
 
• **The narrow-gauge railway** is the railway track, in which **the distance between two tracks **is **2 ft 6 in **(762 mm) and **2 ft **(610 mm).

• **Broad gauge **is also called **wide gauge **or **large line**. The distance **between the two tracks **in these railway gauges is **1676 mm (5 ft 6 in**). It would not be wrong to say that any gauge, **wider than **the **standard gauge **or **1,435 mm (4 ft 8½ inches), **is called **broad gauge**.
 
• The **distance between **the **two tracks **in this railway gauge is **1435 mm (4 ft 8½ in**). In India, **standard gauge **is used **only for urban rail transit systems **like **Metro, Monorail, and Tram**.
